newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL PLAYERS PRAISE GOALSCORER FOWLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL PLAYERS PRAISE GOALSCORER FOWLER.

text.p: Robbie Fowler's lethal finishing could hand Liverpool the passport into a very exclusive club which currently consists of Ajax, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Juventus.

If the locally-born striker, who will not be 22 until next month, continues finding the net with the accuracy he showed three times over the two legs of their European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final against Brann Bergen, then Liverpool could well go on to lift the only European trophy they have yet to win.
And that would enable them to join the quartet of clubs who have won all three European club trophies.
Liverpool have won the European Cup four times and the UEFA Cup twice but their best performance in the Cup Winners' Cup was in 1966 when they finished runners-up to Borussia Dortmund.

Fowler's two goals in Thursday's 3-0 second-leg win over the Norwegians, plus a superbly-taken individual effort in the first leg which ended 1-1, took Liverpool a step nearer the final, helping them cruise through to the last four 4-1 on aggregate.
And his team mates were in no doubt after Thursday's win who had done most to negotiate Liverpool through a potentially difficult encounter which in the end they won comfortably.

Midfielder Jason McAteer, who played with nine stitches in a head wound, said afterwards: "Robbie is in tremendous form. He may have started the season off slowly but he is really scoring the goals now.
"We call him God because he does wonderful things. It is a privilege to play with him."

Defender Steve Harkness, who had a fine match himself, added: "There is no other word I can use to describe him other than phenomenal. Give him a chance and he will get a goal. He is an awesome talent, frightening really."

Liverpool manager Roy Evans added his tribute, saying: "It is nice to see him in the groove. I hope he stays there. We could do with him being on fire until the end of the season, that would be a great boost for us and if other people can score alongside him, that will be an even bigger bonus."
Fowler opened the scoring on Thursday, sending Brann goalkeeper Vidar Bahus the wrong way from the penalty spot after 25 minutes, converting the spot-kick after he had been tripped up in the box.
He then wrapped up Liverpool's victory with a first-time angled left-foot snap-shot after 78 minutes which took his European tally to six in the last four matches.
In all this season he has scored 28 goals and, despite his young age, has scored more than 100 goals for Liverpool in under four seasons.

Liverpool's other goal on Thursday was scored by unsettled Stan Collymore who had luck on his side, scoring off his shin just two minutes after coming on as a 60th-minute replacement for Czech striker Patrik Berger.
Brann threatened to score with several half-chances early on but were always likely to lose after Fowler's opening goal.

Their manager Kjell Tennfjord admitted afterwards: "We had our chances but didn't take them and Liverpool deserved their victory. I don't know much about the other teams left in the competition but Liverpool must have a very good chance of winning it. I think they are the best team in England -- better than Manchester United."
